utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I observe and the Chamber was informed that Mr. Mladic did not want to enter the courtroom. Any explanation, Mr. Lukic? Or Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. We have agreed -- just before the hearing, we have been informed by Mr. Mladic that, in view of the fact that the witness will be heard via videolink today, he believes that, in this way, his rights to directly hear the witness would be violated and he cannot and does not wish to take part in working with this witness in this way. He insisted that we inform you about that. We conveyed to him that examination via videolink is not an unusual situation, but it is exceptional and possible under certain circumstances. We indicated to him the possibility of the hearing being held without his presence. He said that we should convey to you that he continues to insist that witnesses be heard directly in the courtroom in his presence, and therefore he does not wish to enter the courtroom today. Your Honours, it was my duty to convey that to you here today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is clear, Mr. Stojanovic. I put on the record that the Chamber has decided on a motion, which was filed on the 14th of August, 2012, requesting that the present witness be permitted to testify via video-conference link. The Defence has responded to this motion, and although they had some questions about the medical documentation, the Defence did not oppose the request by the Prosecution. The Chamber has decided on the matter in its decision of the 7th of September, 2012. No request for leave to -- to grant leave for an appeal was filed. Therefore, there is a final decision on this matter by the Chamber, and the Chamber cannot understand the position of Mr. Mladic in any other way than that he waives his right to be present at this moment during his trial. If this observation would not be accepted by the Defence, then we would like to know why it is not accepted by the Defence. But as matters stands now, the Chamber intends to proceed in the absence of Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic having waived his right to be present. Any further comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I would just like to ask for a short break so that I can convey this to Mr. Mladic so that we can receive further instructions. We shall then return to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make the following submission. Mr. Stojanovic has said that he informed Mr. Mladic of the possibility we could proceed. Could I ask that Mr. Stojanovic be directed to inform Mr. Mladic that his failure -- that he has the right to be present at his trial under Article 21, and his failure to come out would be deemed a voluntary waiver of that right so he fully appreciates the significance of his failure to come to court. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I understood that Mr. Stojanovic had informed Mr. Mladic about this before we entered court, I will just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may inform the -- Mr. Mladic as suggested by Mr. Groome, although we thought that it would have been done already, but you can do it again. If Mr. Mladic wants to enter the courtroom, he should do that without any further noise. Just come into the courtroom, sit down, and behave. That's what we expect him to do. And that's also the reason why we are willing - exceptionally - to wait with the examination of the witness until Mr. Mladic comes in. If Mr. Mladic doesn't wish to enter the courtroom, please tell us so that we can start. We take a break of two minutes. --- Break taken at 9.40 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we said two minutes. If you have problems in your communication with your client, fine, but then one counsel should stay in court and the other one can deal with it out of court. We said two minutes, and we meant it. Anything to report?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in accordance with what we said, we did speak to Mr. Mladic, and he stood by what he said, that he did not wish to enter the courtroom today while this witness is being examined. He said that that can be considered as his waiver to attend the examination of this witness, and he will appear in the courtroom when we continue examining the witness who was here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least that's the moment where he wishes to attend again, I do understand. Let's first now proceed with the videolink. Is our representative in Sarajevo, I think it is, is she able to see us and to hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. I can see and hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then is the Prosecution ready to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May I take this opportunity to introduce to the Chamber to a member of the team who has not appeared before, Ms. Abeer Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now protective measures are in place - face distortion, voice distortion, pseudonym - but the testimony in itself would be public. Ms. Hasan, that's the position at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. That's correct, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the witness be escorted into the room. And are all the protective measures effective at this moment? Ms. Hellman, at the other side, can you confirm that every preparation for the protective measures has been made?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, I would like to ask my colleague from the courtroom to verify protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could the same be done at this side of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll take a break of ten minutes. --- Break taken at 9.53 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume. Can it be confirmed that all protective measures, that is, voice distortion, face distortion, are in place, and then, of course, we have the use of pseudonyms. Can this be confirmed? Either from the Registry in The Hague or from the other side of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, all the protective measures are in place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Madam Registrar, at the other side of the videolink, could the witness be escorted in the videolink room.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, witness is present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness RM145, can you see me and can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which will now be handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness RM145. Please be seated. Witness RM145, your testimony will be given under protective measures. No one in the public will see your face. No one in the public will hear your own voice. And we'll not address you by your own name, but we'll call you "Witness RM145." Now if you're asked any question, and if you fear that by answering that question in accordance with the truth you might reveal your identity, please do not hesitate to ask me that we go into private session. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you'll now be examined first by Ms. Hasan. Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution. Carefully listen to her questions. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for the record we are relying on certain adjudicated facts in relation to this witness and have redacted portions of his statement accordingly. I won't mention the specific adjudicated facts as -- out of an abundance of caution and for the witness's protection, unless you wish me to do so and we can enter into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we've seen the numbers do appear in the confidential exhibits, which I take it you'll send us soon a statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 28423 displayed on the screens but not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I trust that you see something in a hard copy or on the screen before you? And if I may ask you, without reading anything out loud, to please confirm whether it is your name and your date of birth that is recorded on this paper under RM145?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd offer 65 ter 28423 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 28423 shall be assigned P254, under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P254 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we now have the first page of 65 ter 28422 displayed on our screens. And, again, not broadcast for the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall having met with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 14th of February in 2011 when an amalgamated statement that comprised your prior statements and your prior testimony, as well as additional information, was read to you in your language. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Please take a look at this first page. Do you see your name on it?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature that is on the bottom right-hand side of the English version of this document?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And can you tell me whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Have you recently --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can actually now turn to page 16 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is the last page of the document. Do you recognise the signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is that your --

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you recently had the opportunity to read this amalgamated statement of your evidence from 14th February 2011 in your language?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yesterday we spoke and you informed me that there were three changes you wished to make to your statement, and I will take you through the changes that you spoke to me about. The first one was to paragraph 16 of the B/C/S version, and you wished to replace the word -- the B/C/S word for the English word "nephew" to "tetic" as opposed to "necak"?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you told me that this more accurately reflected your relationship to the named individual in that paragraph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In addition to that there were two changes you wished to make to paragraph 51 of your statement. The first was that the bus that you were on that stopped in Sokolina had the driver, Zuti, plus two guards on it and not three guards, as the statement currently provides. Is that a change you wish to make?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Finally, in relation to that same paragraph, you wanted to correct the statement that there were 50 to 55 of you crammed onto the bus. And you wished to correct that --

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. 55 would be the correct number.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other changes or corrections that you wish to make to the statement?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No. The rest is fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Taking into account these changes, these corrections that we have just made, if you were asked the same questions, would you provide in substance the same answers of the evidence contained in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of this statement, as corrected?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd offer into evidence the witness's amalgamated statement of 14th February 2011, which is 65 ter 28422, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I see that Mr. Stojanovic has no objections, Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 28422 shall be assigned Exhibit P255.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P255 is admitted under seal. Ms. Hasan, may I ask you one -- seek clarification of one small matter. If you would look together with me at page 9, the question starting at line 14, second line where you said "that comprised your prior statements and ..." and there followed two words. I'm trying to reconcile that with ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I -- I understand already the matter that was on my mind due to the help of my colleague, so it is a matter of timing of taking the statement in 2011, which is a while ago, and the present situation. Therefore, there's no need for further clarification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave I'll now read a summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In 1992, RM145 resided in the Novi Grad municipality. In late May, the witness's village was attacked. The attack was led by Jovan Tintor, Nikola Stanisic, and others. Approximately 30 men, including RM145, attempted to escape, and after being ambushed, surrendered. The Serb forces separated RM145 and 13 others from the rest of the group. Jovan Tintor ordered that they be taken to the barracks at Bojnik. On the way, the Serb forces beat, abused, and threatened to kill the Muslim men. Upon their arrival at Bojnik, RM145 saw other prisoners there who had been captured from other villages in the area. The detainees, including RM145, were severely beaten. The Muslim men were then taken to the army fuel depot in Rajlovac. RM145, together with 85 to 90 other Muslim prisoners, were detained in an empty fuel cistern, or reservoir. Mile Stojanovic introduced him as the commander of the camp. RM145's evidence addresses scheduled incident B 10.1. After nine or ten days of his detention in these -- in this fuel cistern which involved repeated beatings and interrogations, RM145 saw Zuti, the driver of Jovan Tintor, and four armed men take out ten prisoners who were told they were going to be exchanged but never returned to the cistern. The next day Zuti returned and called out the name of an additional 15 or 16 men. These men were taken out of the cistern and were also never seen again. Finally, the witness's evidence addresses scheduled incident B 10.2. He describes how on the 14th of 1992, 55 of the prisoners detained in the fuel cistern were put on a bus and told they were being taken to be exchanged in Kobilja Glava. They were escorted by eight men in camouflage uniforms, and two vehicle -- four vehicles; two at the front of the bus and two at the rear. Instead of going to Kobilja Glava, the bus drove in the direction of Semizovac and stopped in a place named Sokolina. The driver and guards got off the bus and moments later the bus was fired at. Those who attempted to escape the bus were shot. Forty seven of the Muslim men on the bus were killed. RM145 sustained an injury to his left arm and is one of the few survivors of this massacre. That concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 05391 displayed on the screens. This is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'd ask you, Witness, if you could tell us what this photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Which of these two cisterns, the one on the right before you, or the left, were you detained in?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I was detained in the left smaller tank, which used to contain petrol. The bigger one contained some 130 men. I don't know why they were in the bigger tank. Later on, they were exchanged at the same time they put us on the buses to be massacred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd seek the admission of this photograph, 65 ter 03591.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I observe that earlier, page 14, line 5, that the 65 ter number, for whatever reason, is not correct. But 03591, the photograph we just looked at, will receive, Mr. Registrar, number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 03591 shall be assigned Exhibit P256. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P256 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, how long were you held captive in this fuel cistern?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: We were there for a fortnight. Or, rather, 13 days. Because the day before the massacre, they had taken us in cooler trucks. They drove us all around Eastern Bosnia, Sokolac, Koran, Rogatica, and then they returned us to Pale. Most probably they did that in order to remove us from that site when the other detainees and women and children were being exchanged on the 13th. On that day, in the evening, they brought us back. So I would say that I was there -- that I was detained there for 13 days, and then on day 14 we were taken to be massacred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: At paragraphs 41 and 44 of your amalgamated statement, you give evidence about a man nicknamed Zuti who came to the fuel cistern and called the names of a number of men who you said you heard were to be exchanged. These men were taken away. Could you clarify for us on how many occasions during your detention did this take place?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Twice. Zuti came twice. As far as I can remember, on the 9th or the 10th of June, 1992, he came and he took away ten men including Brailovic and some others whose names I can't remember. Allegedly, they were being taken to Ilidza to be exchanged. However, I never saw those men again after the war. Some were found in the Vlahovo cemetery in Blazuj. The second time he came, he took away 15 or 16 men from Bioce in the direction of Ilijas, and those men were never seen again either.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we now have a video-clip played, and it bears 65 ter number 22388E.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- do you recognise what was on this clip?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Please tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: That was a bus of the transport company on to which we were loaded from the Rajlovac camp. We had two vehicles escorting us. There were two guards in each of them and Zuti was the driver, and they brought us to the place where you can see the buses, the place is Sokolina. They carried out an all-out attack from all the infantry weapons that they had. They used those against the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In your statement, amalgamated statement, at paragraph 60, you state that a photographer by the name of Ibrahim filmed the entire massacre. Could you clarify whether the video we just saw is the video that you were referring to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd now seek the admission of 65 ter 22388E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to have it replayed and have certain portions, if need be, to be stopped so that we have a still. Judge Moloto will indicate where he would like to have the still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At the stage where we can see the bus closest.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We further continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I -- with your leave, we would have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason for our objection to admitting this part of the video-clip is the following. Or rather, there are several reasons. First of all, we do not have a relevant enough confirmation of the authenticity of the clip. Secondly, the clip is so ambiguous in terms of the vehicle, in terms of the place where the -- we can see the vehicle, as well as in terms of the damage that may be seen on the vehicle possibly. Thirdly, this video-clip, at least according to what we can see as regards the date and the time, is not a contemporaneous video-clip. Actually, it was taken after the tragic event. So it is not a video-clip of the massacre. This is a not a video-clip of the massacre. And it does not serve the purpose for which it has been tendered. That is why we are of the opinion that this part of the video-clip should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "this part." I do not know whether there is a broader video-clip. You suggest so, Mr. Stojanovic. Could you tell us what your understanding is of any remainder we have not seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in our preparations for today's session, I had an occasion to look at the video-clip which is a compilation of several video-clips, it's rather lengthy. And it doesn't comprise only the depiction of this bus but also the journey to the place as well as the burial of the people killed there, and there are also some other portions which are separate from this particular event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to ask one or two questions to the witness before we proceed. Witness, could you tell us when the bus was shot at, when most of the persons on board of this bus were killed, was it dark, was it light? What time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was sometime around half past 6.00 or 7.00 in the afternoon. It was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was still daylight. My next question is, you said this video depicts the massacre. Now, from this video I did not observe anything of shooting which would result, perhaps, in breaking glass or whatever. I do not see any of that. How do I have to understand your testimony? That this depicts the bus on which you were when you were massacred; or that this actually depicts the shooting at the bus when --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The massacre was carried out. I wish to say something. The massacre was carried out on the 14th of June, 1992, late in the afternoon. After the massacre was carried out, I and my neighbours and friends managed to pull through, and I crawled through the area until I reached a Muslim village sometime in the morning. I had been walking through a forest all night. When I arrived at that village, we were received by the villagers, and then the Territorial Defence took two tractors in order to pull out those massacred men, and it was then when the video-clip was taken depicting the bus, the people on the bus, those who had been massacred, and then those people were pulled out from the bus. Dragan Ekanovic came to that place, together with the Chetnik escorts, and he said that he had not seen anything on the bus when the bus passed by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you present -- could I ask you the following question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, were you present when this video was taken the next morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was present when the bodies were being pulled out from the bus and when they were brought to the grave where they were buried. The Territorial Defence and its chief, Dzafer Heric, did not allow me and my uncle to go down there. They feared for our safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you, that next morning, did you see the bus again, which you had left that night before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I was up there. We were up there recovering and all that. All day on the third day of my stay in Vukasevic village where I was being treated by the villagers, there was a doctor there as well. On the third day, that bus was set on fire by Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wish to say is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to focus your answers very much to my questions. You said the day after the massacre, the video was taken. I asked you whether you were present when that video was taken. That means: Were you in the vicinity of the bus, and could you see the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. One second, please. First of all, Ms. Hasan, would you like to respond to the objections to the video being admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The statement in the amalgamated statement that a particular videographer or photographer filmed this video, and it does state there that it is a video of the massacre, which we've always understood it to be a video that was taken the day after the massacre of the bus, and there's another clip we will be showing. These are just excerpts of the entire video which is somewhat lengthy, that we selected, to be displaced here. In terms of -- so in that respect, and on the basis of the witness's evidence, that he recognises the bus that's on the video as the bus that he was in, there is sufficient foundation for its admission. In terms of the place and the damage to the vehicle and what can be seen, it is -- the video is what it is. And it does have the dates -- date stamp there. In terms of -- so there's no disagreement that it is not depicting the actual shooting of the bus from our point of view. And so the purpose of it is to -- the purpose of this clip that we're tendering is to simply see which is what the witness has stated, that this is, in fact, the bus that he recognises as the one he was in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now I think the objection was twofold. First authenticity; second, the place and the identity and the circumstance of all that; and it not being contemporaneous. The latter matter has been dealt with to some extent. Do you know who took the video? Is there information about who took the video, any statement or any?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We'd have to dig in a little bit on that. I have -- I know it was seized in 2002, but I'll have to look a little bit closer into from whom. I know what this witness has said, which it was a photographer called Ibrahim who was present the day after on the massacre -- the day after the massacre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that it will MFI the video for the time being but we may have some additional questions on it anyhow. But, first, a number to be assigned to this video for purposes of it being MFI'd, Mr. Registrar, will be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 22388E shall be assigned P257. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. It will keep the status of marked for identification. Judge Fluegge would have one or more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Witness. Can you tell us a little bit more about the photographer who took the video, according to your testimony. You called him Ibrahim. Can you tell us, do you know this man personally --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have you seen him while he was taking this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met him when he returned after he had taken this video. He resided in Vogosca. He hails from Donje Selo, a village not far from the one where I ended up after the massacre. Since he could not stay in Vogosca, he returned to his native village. He is a photographer by profession. He had a camera on him. He had video cassettes, and he could use that to record the crime. When I set out towards the free territory, I had that video cassette on me. And I would like to say one more thing: That bus is still on that day when -- where -- to this very day, this bus is on the place where the massacre was carried out in Sokolina. Anybody can see it. You can see the damage on the buses, and there's also a commemorative plate which was placed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. What is the family name of this photographer, Ibrahim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, I believe that it is either Dzafic or Heric. I wouldn't know. It was a long time ago. I don't recall. I know that his first name is Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. And what did he tell you at that day how he got there and how he was able to film this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A Territorial Defence unit had already been set up in that village. It had its commander and its members and he was one of them. There was also a doctor there who helped us who had been wounded. He treated us. Dzafer Heric, the then-chief of the regional Territorial Defence, hired him to record what had happened, to record that crime. The Territorial Defence members took two tractors and went down there in order to pull out the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. One final question. How did that happen, that you received this video from this photographer? Why did he hand it over to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, so that I could testify to the crimes committed by those Chetniks against the Muslims, just as I'm testifying here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have a technical problem with the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if the videolink has been restored. Could that be confirmed from the other side of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me ask one final question, another final question. Did this photographer, Ibrahim, hand this video over to you that day or at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on that day when I went to Olovo with my relative in Vares, Visoko, in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you hand this over to the Prosecution or any other institution for the investigation of a crime; and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. About the 28th of December, 1992 I arrived in Hrasnica, and the army in Hrasnica took that cassette from me. When I was to cross over the track at the airport, UNPROFOR would take it and they would return it when they arrived in Sarajevo, when they went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to add that when they came from the Hrasnica press centre to the television in Sarajevo, they called me and returned the tape, but I was told that the tape had been sent to other places abroad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also have one more question. I was a bit uncertain about your answer on when you received this video. You said you received it on the day you entered free territory and, later on, when asked by Judge Fluegge, you said: "It was on that day when I went to Olovo with my relative ..." Now, when was that? Was that immediately after the event? Or was it a week after or a month after? Could you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was 11 days after the massacre. We were recovering in the village of Vukasovici for 11 days. After an 11-day period, when we set off to Olovo -- well, in fact, after five days Ibrahim gave me the tape because we said we were going to Sarajevo and that we would like to have that tape. Five days later, he gave it to us. After he had shot the footage. And on the 11th day, we left the village of Vukasovici and went in the direction of Olovo and further on to Sarajevo. I took that tape with me as far as Hrasnica, which is located in the surroundings of Sarajevo, and it is there that the army said that if I took it over the tarmac, because there was no other way to reach Sarajevo, you had to cross the tarmac, the army said that in that case, the UNPROFOR -- UNPROFOR take it from me. They had some secret routes that they used, and they would use those routes to take it with them, and they would return it to me when I came to Sarajevo. I received that tape at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, would you please focus on my questions only. And if I need more information, I'll certainly ask you for it. What I'd like to know is when he gave you the tape after five days, did you already look at the tape at that time? So did you watch what was on the tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when, for the first time, did you watch what was on the tape you had received from Ibrahim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I arrived in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a man who took me in there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said in Visoko. When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was around the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that some -- close to ten days after you received the video, you watched its content. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 10 or 15 days later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will further wait for further information to receive from the Prosecution. Any further questions, Ms. Hasan? Because we interrupted, more or less -- when you tendered the video, we interrupted your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President. A few more questions. In fact, I was going to play another clip from this same video. It's 65 ter 22388G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please play the other video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, what, if anything, can you tell us about the scenes that we just saw on that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: The video-clip shows the locals performing an exhumation of a mass grave, and they used two tractors to transport the locals of the village of Ahatovici who had been killed. The cemetery they were buried in, the grave they were buried in, is at Ravno in the village of Vukasovici, and that grave is still located there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were you present that day when the massacred bodies were buried, as shown on this video?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, I was there, as well as my uncle, and we had to identify all those who had been massacred. However, there were no documents. They confiscated the documents when we were taken captive, so it was only on the basis of their clothing, on the basis of their footwear that we could identify them. On occasion, we identified someone on the basis of that person's features or face, but this was rarely possible, in fact, as the faces were not always intact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were any of the persons on the video familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was this clip of the video, was this part of the video footage taken by Ibrahim which was subsequently given to you?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would also seek the admission of this video. It comes from the same source as the first one, and we will endeavour to provide also additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 22388G shall be assigned P258, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it will keep that status for the time being. I would, nevertheless, have a few questions again also on this video. Witness, you said -- and could we have -- could we have it played just in the beginning and then have a still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have a still here. Yes. Witness, you told us that the video-clip shows the locals performing an exhumation of a mass grave. First of all, you were not present when this happened, or were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, was it an exhumation? I see that there is a date on this video, which is the 15th of June, in the early afternoon --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's when the work was coming to an end, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it an exhumation? Because if I remember well, the -- what was it -- if it was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- was no exhumation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The massacred bodies had been taken and a grave was, in fact, dug, and they were buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were present when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what you just saw in the video as reflecting what you saw at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The grave is to the left-hand side, in my direction. That's where the grave is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you recognise the scenery and persons and the event --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the entrance to the houses, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, my last question would be: You said you received the videotape, and you watched it approximately ten days after you received it. Was this footage on that same videotape you had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was the portion we saw earlier - about the bus - was that also on the tape you viewed ten days after you had received it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had all the footage on one tape. It included the time when they were taken out of the bus, the massacred people were taken out of the bus, and the time when they were buried in the grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked the video to stop at 12:08 seconds, I take it, from the footage we just watched. Ms. Hasan, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just some final questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, how long after the guards and Zuti got off the bus did the fire begin?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: When the bus came to a halt in Sokolina, they said they had to pour in some water because the engine had overheated. When they got out, they ordered us to remain still. They said they would throw a grenade at us and open fire. About 15 seconds after they got off the bus, you could hear a loud explosion at the front of the bus and then they opened fire from all of their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Osa 79-millimetre -- or rather 90-millimetre hand-held rocket-launcher was used and two Zoljas were used, then they threw in hand-grenades, they opened fire from automatic rifles and machine-guns, and this assault lasted for about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Were there any Serbs in the bus at the time it was fired at?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you and the other survivors got off the bus, did you see the vehicles that had escorted the bus to this location?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see --

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: When they finished shooting -- no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see Zuti or any of the other guards when you eventually got off the bus? Were they present?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No. After they had perpetrated the massacre, they turned the engines on and set off in the direction of Srednje.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In paragraph 52 of your amalgamated statement you gave evidence that Zuti stopped at Srednje on the way to Sokolina and that at that point you could no longer hear the vehicles that had been accompanying the bus up until that point. Later, at paragraph 54, you state that after the attack --

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, Witness, if I can just complete my question and then you can answer. You then state at paragraph 54 that after the attack on the bus, you heard two limousines stop alongside the bus. You heard two men have a conversation. And I just wanted to ask you, based on what you were able to hear or see, can you explain whether the four vehicles that started off escorting you at Rajlovac had, in fact, escorted you all the way to Sokolina?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: When we left Rajlovac, there were four vehicles escorting us. Two at the front; two at the back. I heard the sound of the vehicles accompanying us as far as Srednje. When the bus stopped in Srednje, Zuti, the driver, asked a guard, I suppose, at the check-point how many kilometres remained to Sokolina. As far as I can remember, he said between 6 and 8 kilometres. Zuti closed the window and moved on. But from Srednje to Sokolina, I didn't hear any vehicles behind us accompanying us, so one might assume that those vehicles were full of those Chetniks and they left to lay an ambush at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. I think it's time to take a break. Mr. Stojanovic, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I don't think I'll need much time, and I'll perhaps be able to conclude my cross-examination within one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll take a break, and -- yes, Mr. Groome, anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does the Chamber wish me to make arrangements or ask VWS to return Mr. Selak for this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's a reasonable expectation that we will conclude the testimony of this witness in, well, let's say close to 1.00. And then if Mr. Selak would be available --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that would assist. Madam Registrar at the other side of the videolink, we'll take a break and we'll resume in half an hour from now; that is, 20 minutes to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask Madam Registrar the other side of the videolink, whether the witness can be escorted in the courtroom -- in the videolink room, I should say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness RM145, can you still hear me and see me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put a few questions to you in relation to your testimony today. I would kindly ask you not to mention the name of the place where you hail from because of all of us in the courtroom know which place this is. Thank you. In paragraph 4 of your statement, and the Prosecutor asked you today whether you accepted fully as your own, you say that at one point in time the members of the paramilitary units in the surrounding area, around your village, were issued with uniforms and weapons of the former JNA. You say that they wore these uniforms, and these uniforms bore the insignia with four Ss in Cyrillic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I wish to ask you is the following. How do you, and in which way, assess who is a paramilitary and who was a member of the regular army?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I wish to say to you that when the army received orders to withdraw and to leave the barracks, they took along what was indispensable. However, quite a bit of equipment and uniforms stayed behind in the barracks. And then they gave the local Serbs the barracks and put the barracks at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you make a distinction between members of regular military forces of the Army of Republika Srpska and paramilitaries that you called Arkan's Men, Seselj's Men, and the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. When I was taken prisoner and when I was brought before the barracks in Butile, I considered as paramilitaries those who wore everyday clothing. They had those fur hats with cockades. Then they had white ribbons around their arms, and some wore red berets. That would be it. Some of them wore military uniforms of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement further on, you say that in May 1992 all Serb families that lived in the neighbouring villages - not to mention the names of these villages - had left their homes and moved closer to the military barracks in Rajlovac. You think that they had been ordered to leave their homes so that paramilitary units could establish their own military positions there. Do you remember that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think to this day that the reason why the Serb civilian population left their homes closer -- getting closer to the barracks was precisely this possibility of engaging paramilitaries in establishing front lines?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I'll tell you something. Someone - and I don't know who - said to the Serbs that 500 Green Berets arrived in the village. And that's not correct. I'd really like to see someone take a Green Beret prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But will you agree with me that this was precisely the time when in your village and in the neighbouring village that was populated by Muslims, a Territorial Defence Staff was established and about 150 long-barrelled rifles were distributed?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It wasn't 150 long-barrelled rifles that were distributed. Rather, it was mostly police reservists who were in the village and who used to go hunting, and some of them had pistols and whatever. It was only the reserve police that had long-barrelled rifles. If you consider a hunting gun to be a long-barrelled rifle, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you consider hunting weapons to be infantry weapons, small arms?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No. This is guns that are used for hunting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please let us take a look at paragraph 10 together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P255, Your Honours. It's under seal. Just recently we had it admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at this together, and could you try to explain this to us. Sir, in paragraph 10 of the statement that you say you fully stand by, you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I assume that you do have the English version in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- in order to organise ourselves as best we could, we established a Crisis Staff headed by a certain person. You gave the name there. And you say: "We had about 150 barrels of infantry weapons." Now I'm asking you whether these weapons were given to you or whether you had them from earlier on?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No. These are people who had weapons of their own, either hunting guns or pistols. It was only the reserve police force that had been issued with automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean then by this statement, when you say that you had about 150 barrels of infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Well, I consider all of it to be weapons. However, when you don't have anything else, a hunting gun can be an infantry weapon too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When your village was attacked -- actually, before that, local paramilitary units and members of the former JNA asked you to hand over these weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: There was no mention of weapons. What they said was that men from age 15 to 70 should come to the barracks and that our safety and freedom would be guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before your village was attacked, were you asked to hand over weapons? Was it the former JNA and local paramilitaries that asked you to do that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No. They went about in an APC and said through a loud-speaker that we should surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that way, were you told to hand over weapons?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not hand over these weapons; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I, as an individual, did not even have any weapons. As for the others, since the village had been attacked, there was no need to surrender weapons. They put up resistance as best they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Fighting around your village took two days, from the 27th until the 29th of May. And these attacks continued until the morning of the 29th of May, but they were successfully repelled by your side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: How successful it was is something I cannot say. But during those few days, we had been shelled from all the artillery weapons that the former JNA had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 29th of May, 1992, members of Serb paramilitary forces entered your village; right?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. After the shelling, there was even more shelling in front of the infantry. Paramilitaries entered the village, and behind them were tanks and APCs, and -- and there was general chaos. Everybody tried to flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the direct examination, you mentioned that these were units under the control or command of a man whose name, surname, and nickname, you mentioned. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court who this man is? Is he a military man at all?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: That is Jovan Tintor, nicknamed Joja. I knew him only because his land and his house were about 3 kilometres away from mine, and he used to know my late uncles because they went to school together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that he's not military personnel?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I never said that he was military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To this day, you say that he then led the paramilitaries that attacked your village, or, rather, entered your village.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: When I was taken prisoner, when we were singled out, and when these people were killed, he came wearing a military uniform of the former JNA. And it was the summer JNA uniform, at that, military uniform. He had a cap on, and on this cap there was a five-pointed star.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Among the people who you recognised, as you were retreating, and as you were taken prisoner, you mentioned several names; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would be interested in the following, and I'd like to redress that problem. You mentioned the name of Dragan Koprivica and Arnautovic, Bato. Do you remember these two names?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bato Arnautovic is that the same person as Davor Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because I would like to eliminate the difference that I see in your statement. Please let us look at paragraph 22 together of the statement that was admitted into evidence today; P255.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you say, among other things, when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, paragraph 22 is redacted, so therefore there's no need to look at it together with the witness. The Chamber doesn't know what it says. If there's any matter you'd like to raise which is found there, then you have to introduce it not by reference to paragraph 22, but -- and if you have any concerns about inaccuracies in paragraph 22, there's no need to raise it because we can't read it so we're not bothered by the inaccuracies. But if there's any other reason why you want to address matters dealt with in paragraph 22, then, of course, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I'll take things differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you is this: Am I right in saying that you were present when Dragan Koprivica and Bato Arnautovic opened fire from fire-arms at the Muslims in the second group of detainees and then they slit their throats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to under line something else. Bato is a nickname and Davor is his brother. (redacted) (redacted), and also about Dragan Koprivica. I didn't know them well. When they separated us over there, when they turned up and committed crimes, he told me this is Dragan Koprivica, Bato Arnautovic, and Davor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up a document under seal, 1D272.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's pay attention to the first paragraph on page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is also page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue with that, there's all kind of interference on the English audio channel. I now -- it's 12.00, the bells are ringing. I hear in the background. Could it be taken care of that we do not have this other sound. It can come from Sarajevo; it can come from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm informed that you did not provide the document to the Registry in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is correct, Your Honours. I told the Registrar that we would be using his statement. We have not handed them over. I believe that they're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you would expect them to find it themselves and print it out instead of it being provide it -- provided with it by you? That's, let me say, at least is a wrong understanding of how it works.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. In any case, no. I'll try and avoid that. I'll try to overcome that inconsistency. I'll try to do that through my questions to the witness, with your leave. With your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall whether on the 15th of April, 1993, you contacted the institute for research of inhumane treatments, and did you provide them with a statement to that effect?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you allow for a possibility that in 1993 you provided such a statement to that institute, amongst other institutions?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because I would like to know at any point in time, to the best of your recollection, mentioned the name Davor Arnautovic, instead of Bato when you spoke about these events.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It is possible, but I mentioned both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that both brothers, together with Mr. Koprivica, participated in that act?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No, not both of them. But they were all present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, do you still claim today that when it comes to shooting and the act of slaughter, that either Davor or Bato Arnautovic participated in that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: It was Bato Arnautovic who participated in that together with the Dragan Koprivica. (redacted) addressed them by those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you, in practical terms, did not recognise either of those persons. You are testifying today based on what another person told you about those individuals? Are you -- am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. When it comes to their identification. However, I saw those men and my nephew told me what their names were, and that's what I am calling them today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There's a simple reason why I'm going to put the next question to you. Do you know which paramilitary units those three individuals that you have just mentioned belonged to?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: They belonged to Joja Tintor's unit. When Joja Tintor appeared everybody addressed him as their commander, and they consulted with him about the detainees. They asked him what to do with the detainees. They were Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Chetniks, what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I have in mind those paramilitary units who sported fur hats and cockades on their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. Do you know personally when the Army of Republika Srpska was officially established?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned two more names and, again, the names of two brothers, Goran and Zoran Damjanovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those two were on trial before the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were on trial for the events about which you yourself testify?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those two individuals were found guilty and sentenced?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 12th of December, 2012, there will be a hearing before the human rights court on their appeal?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, listening to your last five questions, is there any dispute about this?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, no. The individuals are named in the statement. In fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, my question is the question -- the last five questions were do you know that they were prosecuted, do you know that they were convicted, et cetera. Is there any dispute about all that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, not from our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, why do you ask this witness on matters which are not in dispute? You could agree on it. Quickest way of dealing with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to respond. First of all, I simply don't know what's not in dispute in view of the examination-in-chief. Secondly, I was not a position to meet with the Prosecutor yesterday afternoon and stipulate on what the witness was going to testify about. In the future, I'll try and do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, it's not without reason that I ask whether there's any dispute, because it's very difficult to imagine that these facts, as court proceedings and judgements, that it's all documented, that -- I -- I hardly could imagine that there would be any dispute about it. Apart from that, I do not know yet what the relevance of it is. So therefore if you say I had no opportunity, I would say next time if you have such -- it's not one question, it's five questions in a row, try to find out. And let's focus on matters which are in dispute. That is what we are primarily here for. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The two individuals you have just mentioned, Goran and Zoran Damjanovic, were they also members of the same paramilitary formation as the Arnautovic brothers and Koprivica?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, let's look at paragraph 34 in your statement, which has been admitted as P255. Here, you speak about those individuals who were in charge of the facility where you were accommodated, the fuel tank. And you say that a person, whose name was Mile Stojanovic, came with another person named Sok and four other persons who escorted them. He came up to the fuel reservoir, he introduced himself as the commander of the camp, and you say that they were dressed in blue uniforms similar to police uniforms. My question is this: Was it your conclusion that people who guarded you were, indeed, members of the police?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: They wore uniforms of the Orao air force institute. Those uniforms were blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know whether they were soldiers or police officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Well, since they wore air force uniforms, in my mind they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are those uniforms similar to police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. That uniform consists of a blue shirt and blue trousers. Sok also sported a cap, and on the cap there was a flag of the former Yugoslavia, and on his shirt, on the right-hand shoulder, he had the same flag on -- on his sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's deal with the part of your testimony when you were taken towards Srednje. You mentioned the village of Sokolina. Could you please tell the Court how far is that village from the place where you were billeted at the time? And I'm referring to the reservoir.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Approximately some 35 to 40 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To your best recollection, how much time did it take you to travel that route on the bus?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is the village of Sokolina on the main road leading from Sarajevo to Olovo or did you have to make a detour?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: As you travelled down the main road and as you arrive in Srednje, you turn left and then you take the old road -- regional road under the bridge in the direction of the stone quarry, which is nearby. The village of Sokolina itself is a village with a sawmill, a barn, and a house on the right-hand side of the road. There is a little stream parallel with the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far is it that from the main road leading from Sarajevo to Olovo?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: About 6 to 7 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of us who are not familiar with the area, could you tell us whether at the time in 1992 it was in the territory under the control of the Serbian forces, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, apparently the connection with Sarajevo has been cut. Therefore, we have to wait until it's there again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the connection has been restored. Could you please restart your last question after I have verified that the witness can hear and see us. Can you see and hear us, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question was how far was it from the main road. You said 6 to 7 kilometres, and then I started putting another question to you that perhaps you did not hear. That question was: Could you help us who are not familiar with the area, could you tell us whether that place at the time of these tragic events in 1992 was under the control of members of the Serbian armed forces or under the control of members of the Muslim armed forces?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Let me tell you the road, the local road from Srednje leads as far as the village of Mokro and beyond to Pale. On the right-hand side -- when you leave from the direction of Srednje, on the right-hand side there were the Serbs or the Serbian villages and the place known as Visojevci. Vogosca was beyond the hill. And on the left-hand side there were the Muslim villages and the Territorial Defence was there. In the vicinity of the village of Vukasovici there was a Serbian village known as Drazevici and the Serbs lived there quite normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you about, and I would like you to assist us if you know the answer, has to do with the place where the tragic event occurred. Was that place under the control of the armed forces of Republika Srpska or under the control of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina? In whose area did this event occur?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: The armed forces of Republika Srpska used that road. And when I survived the massacre, after I had recovered, there's a place from which you can see that road, and there was a carrier from the Army of Republika Srpska that was controlling that road with a jeep escort. But I'd like to add that that road was used to take all goods to Pale and elsewhere. And let me also say that they dug a road from Vogosca through the village of Visojevci and I saw trailer trucks using that road to transport looted goods from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to ask you about. If I've understood you correctly, that road passes through the lines that were under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska, and on the left side under the control of the Territorial Defence and the ABiH forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. But I would also like to add something. That was the case until the massacre occurred. The Muslims and the Serbs were negotiating in the village of Gajavi [phoen] in the police centre. And this was the case until the massacre occurred. When the massacre occurred, these two sides started fighting each other. I also want to say that when I left Vukasovici to go to Visoko, a month or a month and a half later, the inhabitants from Vukasovici and the inhabitants of those Muslim villages fled to Visoko because the Chetniks had taken those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we just move on a little more rapidly, please. Just answer my questions and I'll try to be as simple as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I only wanted to explain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If that's necessary, I'm grateful. My following question: To the best of your recollection, fire was opened on the bus from the front part of the bus, when you're looking in the direction that you were advancing in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. But -- but it was also from the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, to the best of your recollection, how long did this shooting last?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: About 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see any of the men who opened fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I didn't. I was under a pile of dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you weren't able to see them at any point in time. And when you got out from under those bodies, you couldn't see any of the people who had taken part in the shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't see anyone, but I heard everything. When they massacred everyone, they turned their engines on, they came out to the bus. One person from one vehicle told another person in another vehicle to get on the bus and see if anyone was alive, but this person cursed him and said you go and check if you are interested in that, and they closed the door and returned to Srednje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have already spoken about that. My question now is as follows: You don't know and you never found out which formation these men whose voices you heard were members of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I don't know which units they belonged to, but I assume that those who perpetrated the massacre turned their engines on immediately, and someone said that they should check whether anyone was still alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the question, the last one, whether the witness found out the formation these men were members of, was that whether he had seen that? Is that what you intended to ask the witness? Yes. Then it's the third time in 30 seconds that you ask the same question to the witness. The first time he said I couldn't see anything because I was under a pile of bodies. Then you asked him whether he could not see outside who were the perpetrators, and of course the answer was no. And then the witness started elaborating on all kind of things we have found already in his statement and he repeats it, and you let him go. And then you now ask it for the third time. That is not the way the Chamber expects you to conduct the cross-examination and also not to ask how long the shooting lasted if the witness has told us that half an hour ago that it was 15 minutes. There's no need to ask the same again and again and again. Would you please take care that you finish in approximately the time you indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour. But the question was also whether he subsequently obtained any information because we'll be dealing with that. That is mentioned in his statement at a later stage. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's have a look at your statement that you have before you, P255. Let's have a look at the part of your statement, paragraph 55, where you say: "When the locals from Vukasovici arrived at the site of the massacre, they found a Chetnik patrol there with two trucks that were supposed to tow the bus away together with the bodies of the people killed in the massacre. They were told to leave." Can you see that part of your statement? It's paragraph 55.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Paragraph 55. "I saw three neighbours of mine coming after me ... "

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
