utterances.text: Please pay attention to the penultimate sentence and the last sentence in that paragraph where it says the following -- my question in fact is since we understand that you didn't go back there, who went to the scene? Members of the ABiH or, as you say, a Chetnik patrol with two lorries?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: A Chetnik patrol arrived with two lorries. Heric Dzafer told me about that when he had returned with the tractors and the massacred bodies. He said he had come across the Chetniks and he had also seen Dragan Ikanovic among them. He was standing there and he said that he hadn't taken part in the incident and that he hadn't seen anyone in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you explain for the benefit of the Chamber how it is possible, if that is what they told you, because I know that you weren't at the site yourself, how is it possible for a Chetnik patrol to arrive then tries to remove the bodies, and at that point in time members of the ABiH arrive from the village of Vukasovici, and no incident occurs? What in fact happened?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: There was no incident because they had been negotiating up until that point in time, and when they arrived there, Heric Dzafer, the chief, said they should be removed because there were 30 members of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were armed. He told Dragan -- or he asked Dragan, What have you done, Dragan? And Dragan replied and said he didn't know anything about it. He then said they should be removed, the bodies should be taken so that they could be buried. And then he said, Dragan, we have living witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you now telling us that after the event the patrol of Chetniks with their vehicles left the bodies to members of the ABiH and they withdrew from the site without a fight?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because the Territorial Defence was more powerful so they couldn't do anything. They returned three days later and they set fire to that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The vehicle you said was an armoured personnel carrier and controlled the road. Could that vehicle have gone into action at that place, at that site where these two groups from the warring factions were present?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: At the time, this personnel carrier was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to the Chetnik units and patrols that you have mentioned, did these patrols discuss the identity of those who participated in the crime?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Dragan Ikanovic told Heric, Dzafer that Boro Radic and Ratko Adic were involved in the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Do I understand you well, Witness, that all what you're telling us what happened at that moment when the TO came and wanted to remove the bodies, that's all hearsay. You were not present, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you can ask the witness what he was told. But to say what did whom, at what time, et cetera, for -- as a question to someone who was not present is -- well, is at risk to produce unreliable evidence. So please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I put my question to you I was aware of the fact that you weren't present. But as I will shortly be concluding my cross-examination, I would just like to ask you the following. The second clip that we had a look at today, and you said in relation to that clip that you were present when the footage was taken of the grave being dug and of the burial, could you tell us whether this footage was taken in a continuous way? Did the cameraman shoot the footage continuously?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I don't know whether he used up one cassette and then put another cassette in the camera. I don't know. But the cassette that he gave to me had footage of the entire event from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the cassette that he gave to you, were there any chronological interruptions?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Well, there were interruptions. He would shoot one scene and then there would be a cut and then he would shoot another scene, so, yes, there were such interruptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had several cassettes or was there only one cassette that he gave to you?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: I do not know. But he gave me one cassette five days later, after he had processed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this cassette was copied in the village when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: He had to copy it because the camera has a small cassette and he to copy that footage onto a large cassette.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the burial of these victims done on the same day when the bodies were collected from the site where they were killed?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. They were brought in in the morning and the bodies were buried on the same day. That was on the 15th in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you ever told that any parts of the video footage were erased?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to have a look at another clip again from the video that we've already had a look at. It's 65 ter 22388G, and I would just like to ask the witness to explain -- provide us with some explanations concerning this segment. And I'd like to view the clip from the very beginning and up to the 39th second of the clip. Could we please see the clip now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're following this footage, I would like to ask you, Mr. Witness, to focus on the lower left-hand corner where you will see the time and the date of this video-clip. You will see the time and date of the video-clip there. Please focus on the 36th second of this video-clip, and then I'm going to ask you to explain this to us. Since you said that you had been there, so you will tell us how come this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, for the transcript, we see the time as 13:58. And could we please go on now. Three more seconds to go. We can stop now, and the time here is 14:41. Bearing in mind what we saw, I would like to ask you the following. This interruption and after that the continuation of this filming, some 50 minutes later, was that the result of a total interruption in the filming or was it the result of the removal of part of this film?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: No, this was interrupted. The man took a rest for an hour. He ate and things like that. So he took a bit of a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I will conclude with the following question. Do you know whether to this day anyone, before any court, was tried because of what you testified about today, because of the deaths of these people on the bus?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the possible perpetrators were tried before any court of law?

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: Yes. Well, no, not perpetrators, but rather those who took part in this from when I was taken prisoner. It was the Damjanovic brothers, Goran and Zoran. And they were convicted, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: RM145
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Hasan, any need for further questions? But let me first consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the document, I think it was 1D272 or something like that, which you had on the screen but which was not provided to the representative in Sarajevo, you hardly used it with the witness, I think. May we take it that you do not intend to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. And I accept the fact that this is an omission on my part. We hadn't submitted it on time. I quoted it, so it will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any further questions for the witness. However, I wanted to raise the issue of the video footage again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we need the witness for that? I mean, if you consider it possible that it would trigger further questions to the witness, then please do it now. If you say, no, that's unimaginable, then we could first excuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think we can excuse the witness at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness RM145, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to the videolink room and for answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Judges. I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I also wish you all the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The representative of the Registry in Sarajevo, we can conclude the videolink at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, given all the questions that were asked and the evidence that's now on the record, it's the Prosecution's position that there's a sufficient foundation for the admission of MFI P257 and MFI P258, both excerpts of a video taken -- taken by an individual we have heard named Ibrahim. The witness has given evidence that he received the video from -- from the -- from Ibrahim shortly after it was taken. He watched the video just a few days after that. He has testified that the events depicted or the scenes depicted on the video reflected what saw when he was present at the scene the day after. He recognised the bus as the one that he was in that was shot at. He recognised the location. And it is, in our respectful submission, what it pour puts to be, a video taken the day after the massacre depicting the bus the witness was in and the removal and burial of the bodies that same -- the subsequent day, on the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that mean that you withdraw your offer to provide us with the information about when it was seized, where it was seized, from whom it was seized? The Chamber would like to have complete information on all aspects regarding authenticity. For example, whether it was the same tape or whether this was a copy or that -- we do not know yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We're still investigating that, and we will provide that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll wait for that information. Then there are a few procedural matters I'd like to briefly deal with. We could then take a break and then we could resume the examination of Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was informed that he would be here from 12.30 so that should be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's ... First, yesterday I dealt with MFIs P80 and, as I said at the time, P89. These are the exhibits which were tendered through Witness van Lynden. I admitted these two and the Defence stated that they had no further objections to it. Now I made a mistake there. I read P80 and P89, but the issue was about P80 up to and including P89. I made a mistake there. May I take it, in the absence of any further comments, that the withdrawal of objections concerned P80 up to and including P89?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I hereby put on the record that P80 up to and including P89 are admitted into evidence. I briefly turn to Witness RM066. The Defence was given time until yesterday midday to make submissions on the MFIs P186, P188, up to and including P190 and P192. The Chamber has not received any submissions. Is the Defence ready to make submissions or does it not wish to make any further submissions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not that we don't wish. And obviously we missed the deadline. And right now, I have no idea, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please look at it during the next break so that we can see and hear what your position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now moving to the other side, talking about deadlines, the Prosecution was given until Monday this week to provide updates on its plans for -- for its plan for 92 bis and 92 quater motions, but I don't think the Chamber has received anything of the kind. Or did we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding was, that's why I'd said last week that I was prepared to give those orally on Friday, I thought the instruction to us was to give those orally. I'm prepared to give them at any moment that the Chamber has some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to hear them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think they're of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, they're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know how much time it takes, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think it may take about 20 to 30 minutes to give a detailed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's quite a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I withdraw the offer to make those submissions at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- could I say to the Chamber that it appears that the way things have progressed this week that we will not have a witness for the -- that will fill the entire hearing time this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll then at least have further time to hear your submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'm ready at any time to make them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then one of the things I had forgotten to put on the record is that the request for leave to reply in relation to Witness RM145, that the Chamber had decided to granted that request for leave. It was filed on the 31st of August, I think, in relation to the Defence response on the 92 ter motion. It's hereby put on the record that leave to file this reply is granted and hereby put on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know off the top of my head whether that was one of the situations where we attached the draft reply or the reply as an annex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you had in your -- you attached it -- well, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll check that over the break, Your Honour, and I will [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I could look it up. Let me see whether I can do it right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was, Mr. Groome, Prosecution reply to Defence response to Prosecution 92 ter motion RM145. And you already included in this reply that you were of a different opinion as to whether the statement included inappropriate opinion or expert evidence, and you more or less repeated in that reply the position the Chamber had expressed in various decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll await your decision then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, we -- it's hereby put on the record that your request for leave to reply is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I meant to await the decision on the underlying application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The underlying application was to have admitted into evidence this statement of Witness RM145, which has been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Oh. I'm sorry, I'm confused. I think I need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'll have a break. Unless there's any other procedural matter at this moment, I would like to take a break until quarter past 1.00 and then resume for one more hour. We'll take that break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, are you ready to, once the witness is back in court, to resume the examination -- I'm sorry, I have to address the Defence. I needed a break as well. Is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Selak? Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, we left off during the last hearing with a matter about whether the witness had to answer a question, yes or no. I'll first deal with that matter before we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And before I give an opportunity to Mr. Lukic to resume his cross-examination, I will give a decision by the Chamber on whether or not you had to answer a certain question. A question aiming at enabling the examining party to obtain further information which it wishes to use for further investigation or exploration of the matter at stake can be relevant. The Chamber considers that the names of other members of the resistance staff in Banja Luka over which the witness said he was elected as commander in the middle of July of 1992 as a lead to further investigate or explore the mistrust the Serbian side may have had of the witness is of hardly any or no relevance to the determinations the Chamber will have to make in this case. The Chamber has considered in this respect that the witness was elected only when he had retired or was about to retire from what had, by then, become the Army of Republika Srpska. The concern of the witness for the other members of the group would, in itself, be no reason not to answer questions that are put to him but an obligation to answer only exists if those questions are sufficiently relevant. The question put by Mr. Lukic is not. And now I address you, Mr. Selak. The Chamber allows you, as you may have heard by now, the Chamber allows you not to answer the question that was put to you. But please keep in mind that the Chamber determines whether or not you have to answer a question and whether or not such answer can be given in private session. You may address the Chamber on these matters, but it is not for you but for the Chamber to decide on the concerns you may have. This concludes the decision of the Chamber. Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Colonel Selak.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please briefly see document P249 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While waiting for it to appear, Colonel, the document is a map, a sketch made by an officer from the 1st Krajina Corps. Now with regard to the first map that we have, you mention the names of the towns where members of the 1st Krajina Corps were deployed, and we're dealing with the 18th of May, 1992, which is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, were there any Croatian units present in Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally do not know, but it was possible because Slavonski Brod is nearby. I didn't have precise information, but the corps command would probably have discussed such an issue at the meetings that it held. I'm not sure but it's possible because the border with Croatia is located there, and I assume that the units entered Bosanski Brod and Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this also go for Derventa which is to the south of Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no Croatian units in Derventa. My opinion is that there were no Croatian units in Derventa. That is what I'm claiming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you avoid to speak simultaneously. If Mr. Lukic intervenes in your answer, it may be because he has -- he considers that he has already received an answer to the question and wants to stop you. Then you should carefully follow Mr. Lukic. He is the one who is in -- conducting the examination. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed. But don't speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, you can see Doboj. It's even further to the south from Derventa, and it's about 70 kilometres from the border with Croatia. At the time, did you have any knowledge according to which Croatian army units had entered about 15 kilometres in the direction of Doboj and they were staying in Bosanski Brod and Derventa and going further south?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me repeat what I said: I have no information according to which Croatian units entered the town of Derventa and, in particular, the town of Doboj because of large garrisons of the Army of Republika Srpska there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you exclude that possibility or do you allow for such a possibility?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I exclude the possibility. That's the information I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Thanks. Let's see the second page in this document on the screen, please. Here, you spoke about the Serbs from Bosnia and the Serbs from Serbia and Montenegro. And you used an X to mark a Serb from Bosnia and two Xs to mark a Serb from Serbia and Montenegro. And the time-frame we are talking about is after the 18th of May, 1992. People from this chart were said to be members of the 1st Krajina Corps Command. In the second row in large box, we can see the name Milan Tomovic, colonel. Do you know that Tomovic was married with a woman -- or to a woman from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then at the same level in the chart, we have Dragan Marcetic. Are you aware of the fact that he is married to a Muslim women from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he remained in the town where he lived with his family. The following person is Miroslav Rankovic, Colonel Miroslav Rankovic. Are you aware of the fact that he left the Army of Republika Srpska when a corridor was created?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date. I know that he went to Serbia, probably to Belgrade. As to his reasons, I don't know what they were. He was the chief of the personnel department in the corps command and personnel officers regularly went to Belgrade because Belgrade would send their officers in. Belgrade directly exerted an influence on the appointment of officers in respective armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were people able to leave Banja Luka, go to Serbia, and do this before the creation of the corridor on the 28th of June, 1992? Was it possible to go?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the time as commander of the logistics base, I myself insisted on the creation of that corridor. It was difficult to pass through because our vehicles, the vehicles the logistics base had, couldn't bring in ammunition and other equipment from Serbia and Montenegro. So it was essential to create this corridor, but even before the corridor was created, vehicles used various routes in order to reach Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just to avoid any confusion, if you look at page 65, line 12, you said here you spoke about the Serbs from Bosnia and the Serbs from Serbia and Montenegro. Now, the legend is Serbs not from Bosnia and Serbs from Serbia Montenegro. At the top. Now, if there's any confusion created by this legend --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... on my part, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously there is. On my part, at least, there is a confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, having been reminded of it, be -- clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, this chart is in English so perhaps whoever made it missed out on something. The first X says Serbs who are not from Bosnia marked with one X, and marked with two Xs Serbs from Serbia and Montenegro. Next to one X should it say, should it read, "Serbs from Bosnia," or "Serbs who are not from Bosnia"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first X was to mean Serbs from Bosnia and Herzegovina; was to stand for Serbs from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Your Honour, could I add something with regard to this issue. There is a [indiscernible] important piece of information that relates to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have clarified this issue for the time being, and as the Chamber said we'll deal with the statements later. I'd just like to go through the list of these names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak aloud. He wants to consult with counsel, if there's any need to do that. Then we proceed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Miroslav Rankovic, Colonel Miroslav Rankovic, did not leave the VRS in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I'm not sure, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following person, Colonel Lazo Kosanovic. Is it your testimony today that he did not leave the VRS in the summer of 1992? He's on the chart below Rankovic.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see him. I personally know this colonel. However, I did not communicate with him after my hand-over of duty as commander of the logistics base. I would see him in Banja Luka, but I don't know the exact dates. The chart changed. People were appointed to other duties. As to where they went -- as to whether they remained within the VRS, I do not know. But I'm claiming there were very few officer who left the Army of Republika Srpska, who left the former JNA. Only those who were to go into retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next box we have, the big one, in the first line - it's the first one to the left - it says Colonel Ratko Simic. Is it your testimony today that this colonel did not leave the VRS in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it refresh your memory if I said that Novica Simic took over his duties, was appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't think what position Ratko Simic was appointed to. I left and -- well, if you had asked me at the time, perhaps I could have answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether he left or did not leave?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next person, the second one on the right from Simic in the same row, it's Celeketic, Colonel Celeketic. Is it your testimony today that he did not leave Republika Srpska in the summer of 1992 after the corridor had been opened?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Celeketic. I have to think about this. I don't think he did. Perhaps in the Autumn, but he did not leave in the summer. I was performing my duties up until the 10th of July, and after that date I didn't move around town that much afterwards. I don't think he left in the course of the summer. He was the commander of the 16th Brigade in the Kozara barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, according to what you can remember, he left in the Autumn not the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably -- he had probably fulfilled the conditions for going into retirement so he left then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What -- Mr. Selak, what is Colonel Celeketic's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel Celeketic. It's not Rade. I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also would have one question in trying to understand - Mr. Lukic, sorry to interrupt - this chart. We have two categories, a Serb, as we now understand from Bosnia, and a Serb from Serbia Montenegro. Now we also find a lot of boxes with names but without any indication. Does that mean that they are not Serb, or does it mean that they are Serbs but not from Bosnia and not from Serbia Montenegro? For example, Serbs from Croatia. Or -- how do I have to interpret the boxes where no indication is given, as we find it in the legend? For example, General Talic. He is not marked as a Serb from Bosnia. He is not marked as a Serb from Serbia Montenegro. What does that mean? Or would you not know? It's a bit unclear to me. Mr. Selak, could you clarify, especially the empty boxes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I took part in making this schematic. This is a mistake. Because Momir Talic, the late Momir Talic, unfortunately, it is a well known thing that he is from Bosnia, from Bosanska Krajina. And it's probably my mistake and the mistake of the team that worked on this. People knew exactly who came from where. So it's just a mistake in making the diagram. Talic is from the area of Banja Luka, as a matter of fact from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you similarly also know where Colonel Vukelic came from or Colonel Stevilovic? Or all those who are without any marking as to their origin, does that mean that you are aware but that it's just forgotten to put it in the chart? And I'm not asking you to go through every single person, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically, Colonel Radivoje Tomanic is from the area of Brcko from Bosnia-Herzegovina. My mistake when making this. Gojko Vojnovic is also from Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know exactly from which town or village but also from Bosnia-Herzegovina. Stevilovic I think is from Serbia. But that's a mistake, Your Honour. I'm not sure I can give a specific answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps for some you would know, for others you would not know. But it's not reflected in the chart. Mr. Groome, of course this sheds some light on the usefulness of a chart where half of the information is left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I -- I accept that, Your Honour. And perhaps maybe the best thing to do would be to limit its probative value to the organisation of the different people and the positions they held if that's what the witness is -- all he is able to verify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say apart from background, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think probably, and I can do it on re-direct, just explore with the witness whether he is certain about the positions they held and their relationship to each other. If I -- it seems that at this point there is a lack of clarity on ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see that. And then last question still about this. At the bottom of the chart, we see the commander of the Derv. Brigade which I take it is the Derventa Brigade. Is that understood? And is that -- U/K major, does that mean that it's an unknown person which held the rank of major? I mean unknown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, a major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of whom you do not know the name, is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I forgot it. Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I've clarified a few matters in relation to the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be zoomed in a bit so the witness can see it better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, well, Mr. Selak, if at the end of your testimony important matters have been left out, you will have an opportunity to add them. But at this moment, I would prefer that Mr. Lukic puts his next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one more thing: Colonel Nikola Obradov is registered here quite clearly. Did he stay on after the summer of 1992 as a member of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him personally. He was the commander of the rocket brigade, the only one in the former Yugoslavia. While I was commander he had stayed on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You start telling us about the rocket brigade, et cetera. The question simply was whether he stayed after the summer of 1992 as a member of the army. Could you please focus your answer on that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it jog your memory if I were to tell you that he was replaced by Rapajic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not sure. I don't know the date when it was. There was a replacement. Now, was it 1992 or later? I'm not sure. There were a lot of transfers among the officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your testimony today, are you sure -- are you not sure that he stayed after the summer of 1992 as a member of the 1st Krajina Corps or the Army of Republika Srpska in general?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not a member of the corps in Banja Luka. Rather, he was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Both speakers are speaking at the same time. We cannot discern what is being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you speak at the same time, we do not have double information but we have no information at all. So try to avoid that. And, Mr. Selak, try to focus on the question. Now, apparently the issue was, and -- yes. Whether that -- and I -- even the name is lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikola Obradov, was he a member of the Army of Republika Srpska after the summer 1992? You said yes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, briefly, this chart is not proper. Not even in terms of which Serbs from Serbia and Montenegro were members of the Army of Republika Srpska after the opening of the corridor on the 28th July 1992, and it's not good in terms of showing which persons held which particular position in the Army of Republika Srpska at that point in time because we see that quite a few of them had left. We are going to prove that very easily. That can easily be seen from the personnel records. So at this point in time we object. Since we now had time to check this, at this moment we do object to the veracity of this piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two matters. The first is what happened -- yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I rise only to say that this is something that clearly the Prosecution has been willing to enter into discussions with to agree to for many months, in particular with respect to the expert Richard Phillips. The only thing really that is a matter there is the organisational chart, so I think I renew my invitation to Mr. Lukic to sit down. We have military analysts, he has people that can he check for the information. I'm sure it's something that we could agree on, an accurate chart of the organisation of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the second of my observations. The first one is questions are put did he stay after the summer or did he stay after this moment or that moment. The chart reads officers -- "offices," I take it that should be "officers," and senior officers of the VRS 1st Krajina Corps, after the 18th of May, 1992. Now, today is after the 18th of May of 1992. But I do not expect that this chart expresses the situation of today. So therefore, in order to understand it and to also understand whether its inaccurate or not, it may be relevant to know who stayed after the 18th of May but also how long he stayed and without an end date or without further dates. And here and there we have a bit of a date. For example, for Stevilovic, it says 06/92 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was killed. Okay. That's clear that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's not clear for us, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It just gives a -- it just gives a date. He could have married on that day or he would have resigned or -- I mean, why -- the Chamber, of course, wants to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- understand the evidence. And, Mr. Lukic, again I'm primarily addressing at this moment Mr. Groome, but at the same time questions to be put about what happened in the summer, whether that contradicts the chart, is very difficult to establish because the chart doesn't given any further information as the -- I just want the parties to keep this in mind. Both when supporting or when criticizing the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just add that I think some of the confusion is this witness left in the middle of the summer and I think it might reduce the confusion if we're -- if the question is posed whether -- while he is there or does he have knowledge about what happened after he left. I think that may reduce some of the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, middle of the summer. I do understand that the witness left mid-July. If that's the middle of the summer, then it could be more precise. But I just share with you my concerns in how we should understand and interpret this piece of evidence. My second observation would have been is there no possibility to agree on most it. But that is already raised by Mr. Groome. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Why I am challenging -- sorry, I have to come back to this issue. Why I am challenging this chart is because the -- one of the main points of this witness's testimony is that Serbs from Serbia stayed in the VRS and it still remained part of JNA. So the same army. And we exactly showed, and we will show, that it's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we're looking forward to that evidence and that challenge to the chart. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please go on dealing with paragraph 61 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution please provide the witness with a copy of the statement. [In English] To the witness. Yeah, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this paragraph, Colonel, have you found it? Paragraph 61. In it, you say: "At that point in time, in Bosnia-Herzegovina" -- or, rather, "in the Bosnian Krajina there was no Bosniak or Croat army." That's what you say. "Hence it is not possible that the prisoners in Manjaca camp had been arrested during military combat." My question is as follows: Is it your testimony today that in Krajina there wasn't any armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. There were armed conflicts because in municipalities in Bosanska Krajina units were formed to protect the people. There were hunting guns there and also weapons were bought from Serb neighbours, because they had received it from members of the JNA. I have a document to that effect. How many weapons were distributed by the JNA and by the SDS to the Serb people. As a matter of fact, they would write in big capital letters "Srpska" on houses because -- because weapons were distributed at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I ask you what time it is and you say to me it is Wednesday today, that is not an answer to my question. You really have to focus on what it is that I am asking. I'm not saying that your information is not correct, but please focus on my question and answer that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the army did not exist as such, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of Bosanska Krajina. There was only groups that organised resistance in municipalities and local communes in order to protect themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. That is what you claim when say that there was no army in the territory of Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was covered by the Banja Luka Corps with the exception of Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. It's clearer now. You mean that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we please have the document P244 on the screen. It would help all others --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now move onto paragraph 63 of your statement, please. This is what you say. Reported signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Stanimir Djurovic, dated the 1st of June, 1992. "In Prijedor, Kljuc, and Sanski Most, our units successfully conduct the mop-up of the terrain without encountering any strong resistance and capturing large numbers of both the paramilitary rank and file." In parenthesis it says about 7.000 so far. In the very next paragraph your comment is as follows. So this is paragraph 64, you say: "This report is of interest because there could not have been 7.000 paramilitaries there. It is my belief that they were civilians." My question: At the time, did you go to these areas that are described in this report, Prijedor, Kljuc, Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go but I did have information from my co-workers and friends and also documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Which friends? What information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friends from Banja Luka, officers as a matter of fact. Because I stayed on in Banja Luka, I continued to live there, and my colleagues, officers, Serbs --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which officers told you this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Selak, the last question was whether you went there, I think. That was the previous question. Did you go to the area? You said I did not go. That's an answer to the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you started telling other things. Well, if Mr. Lukic would be interested, then he would ask you for that. Now, then Mr. Lukic asked you what -- which friends, what kind of information? And then you said friends from Banja Luka, officers as a matter of fact. That's an answer to the question. And then you say because I stayed in Banja Luka, I continued to -- The question was: Which friends, what information. Yes? Could you please resume your answer there. Which friends? By category or by name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Friends, Serbs, officers, colleagues of mine who lived and worked in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What information did you receive from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked about the situation in terms of combat operations, when the war would be over, what all of this was leading to, and as friends and colleagues and patriots they told me what their opinions were and what was happening in Bosanska Krajina and, in particular, in the Banja Luka Corps. That is the information that I had. And I trusted them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was very specific about the number of troops. What did they say about numbers? Numbers of paramilitaries? Did they say anything specific about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they did not say that specifically. However, I analysed after the war the combat operations as they evolved in municipalities, and we came to certain conclusions in the Institute for War Crimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. Because my question was, did they say anything specific about that. Your answer was: They did not say that specifically. That's an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I was really interested to know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how you nevertheless came to certain figures, I would ask you. And we'll see what Mr. Lukic further wants to ask you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So these colleagues of yours at that time did not tell you about any numbers, and we'll also deal with the subject of arming these areas because you claim to know the numbers of personnel and weapons. Let me ask you now: Did you take part in the arming of Muslims in the area of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that armed Muslims in the area of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that you then cannot even speak about who had which quantity of weapons?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such information did not exist even in the corps. This is a fabrication of people from these units that were cleansing these municipalities of Muslims. That's the point. And that is what matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who invented this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who provided information according to which there were 7.000 armed paramilitary troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units from the VRS that covered that territory. That's their report. This is a report from the corps according to which there were 7.000 of them. Where they did obtain that information? The Muslims didn't provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you obtain information that there weren't that many? That's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there had been so many of them, a unit with 4.000 men couldn't have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is all hypothetical. Do you have information or not? That's all I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again, this is not a debating club. This is a court of law. Carefully listening to what Mr. Selak says is, to the extent people have said that there were 7.000, I don't believe them, although I myself have no direct observation of any numbers. Neither were specifics given by the persons I consulted at that time about those numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you. [Interpretation] Could we now see -- just a minute. Could we now see document -- it doesn't have a number yet. 09041 is the number. [In English] One minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the document on your screen dated the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document states that anti-army propaganda has reached unprecedented dimensions. This propaganda has reached unprecedented dimensions. This propaganda is led by the Party of Democratic Action and Alija Izetbegovic personally. Yesterday you agreed that some political parties, not all of them, were active against the JNA. Is it true that some of the active-duty officers moved over to the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that point in time, as early as then?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had been established in March 1992. It had been recognised by the international community and the JNA was a foreign force occupying the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you, too, at the time felt as if you were a foreign force occupying the area?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Understand this as you will, but I remained a patriot in respect of all three peoples. Not just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it logical to expect that the JNA could immediately leave Bosnia and Herzegovina at the same time that Bosnia and Herzegovina had been declared to be an independent state?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The JNA units in Bosnia and Herzegovina were renamed the Army of Republika Srpska on the 18th of May, 1992 - all of the units - and they remained present in the areas that they had previously occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have already asked you about this and you have answered my question. You said that the local people were now in those units. The young men doing their military service who weren't from Bosnia and Herzegovina left the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you confirmed this?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So whether a unit is called this way or that way, whether it changes its name or not, it doesn't matter. But the fact is that instead of a soldier, a 19-year-old soldier who came from Belgrade, there was a 45-year-old man from Prijedor who took his place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, whether a unit is called this way or that way, whether it changes its name, it doesn't matter, or didn't matter. But the fact is that's not questions. That is argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then at the very end you asked do you agree with me. Take it proposition by proposition, and then clearly ask the witness what you'd like to hear from him. And apart from that, if you say, It doesn't matter, and if you say, Do you agree with me, then you are asking, you're inviting the witness to say whether something matters or not. Well, that's not for a witness of fact to answer. So therefore try -- I do understand it's not easy. Let me say this as well. But try at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to keep it organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's enough, but I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not criticise you for not doing your best but I'm trying to assist you in performing your duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let me ask you the following: Is it true that the units of the former JNA changed their names?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the units of the former JNA changed their troops? I'm not talking about the officers. We have already discussed who remained and who left. But did the troops, the soldiers, change?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only partially. A small number of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A small number of soldiers, of privates, in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So all those soldiers from the VRS who were over 23 or 24 years of age had previously been in the JNA in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A 45-year-old man from Banja Luka served in the JNA, from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son had -- was 20 years old and he did his regular military service in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He was from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about people over the age of 23 or 24.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They also did their regular military service?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Someone who was 45 years old did his military service, his regular military service in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time. There was a mobilisation later. Let us understand each other. When there was a mobilisation, everyone up to the age of 60 had to report to military units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll return to this document that we have before us dated the 14th of April, 1992. Is it true that entire staffs of the Territorial Defence went over to the side of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not entire staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The entire staff, for example, in Visoko, in Konjic, did these staffs move over to the side of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because this was covered by the ABiH, so Croats and Bosnians responded. There were also Serbs who were members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that military facilities at that time - on the 14th of April, 1992 - were targets in Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm not only referring to the 1st Krajina Corps. We know that wasn't the case there. Were military facilities targets for attacks? Do you have any such information? Was this the case in certain parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina where the Muslim inhabitants were in the majority?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such acts because the former JNA was on the side of Republika Srpska. So it was a revolt and there were such activities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And were military facilities in Croatia also attacked before these attacks?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I assume that that is possible but I'm not certain, so I can't answer your question precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time on the 14th of April, 1992, did the JNA attack the Muslims or Croats in any part of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such information, so I couldn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time were flats of members of the JNA in Bosnia and Herzegovina also attacked? Were military personnel arrested, taken captive?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people would abandon their flats, flee from the territory covered by the armija. Covered by the Federation right now. At the time it was Bosnia and Herzegovina. Officers, citizens, Croats, and Serbs would flee. They would exchange positions or, rather, their places of residence. Your Honours, I have a document. In Banja Luka there was an order according to which Muslims from the Crisis Staff had to leave Banja Luka and they weren't allowed to return to their flats. So this certainly took place in other areas as well, but I don't have any precise information as to where, to what extent, and at what time such things occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 2 in the B/C/S version, under number 1, we can see what was insisted on in the JNA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is also page 2 in the English version, item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We receive no interpretation at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under number 1 it states: "Maintain unity of the army, especially of officers. Talk openly with all JNA members." I'll start again. "Maintain unity of the army, especially of officers. Talk openly with all JNA members." In brackets it says AVS and GL. It means active-duty officers and civilians. "We don't want any vacillation or treachery. Everyone should make clear where he stands beforehand, and it should be stated clearly that the army was brutally attacked and had not done anything to harm any of the peoples."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just rise to -- it would -- I think -- I believe it would be more appropriate for the witness to be asked to give abbreviations rather than for Mr. Lukic to provide evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll first clarify this up. My colleague is quite right. Could you first tell us what AVS stands for and what GL stands for?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: AVS means active-duty officer and GL means civilian personnel. This is in reference to the JNA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that at this moment. We have to leave it to that, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Selak -- could you give us an indication, Mr. Lukic, as to how much time you would still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Definitely at least the whole day tomorrow. I don't know if we have some time, and I think that we do, on Friday -- I might take some time from Friday, as I announced seven hours for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further witnesses available for this week, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour. One more witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one. One. And that witness would take?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's -- I don't have the estimates in front of me, but it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll look at the estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It'll be one of the shorter witnesses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, let's try not to lose ourselves in debates and let's try to elicit evidence the witness can really provide to us. I will try to assist you. Mr. Selak and Mr. Lukic, addressing both of you, I was close to the point, which did not often happen during my years in this Tribunal, where I would be the traffic light; that is, no one speaks unless I've given permission. That is stop to this, stop to that, like a traffic policeman, saying, You can now drive. We're close to that point. I just want to inform both of you. And please keep that in mind and try to avoid that I have to serve here as a traffic police officer rather than a careful listener to what the evidence is about. Mr. Selak, I would like to again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and also not to communicate in any other way about that. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 27th of September, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I. But the witness may first leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
